subject: Don't tap that package text, plus 2 quick wins
preheader: A scam to spot, an easier-to-read phone, and a trick with AI.
intro: Welcome to The Bridge Bulletin. Every Monday you get one scam to watch for, one useful tip and one AI trick, in plain English.

sections.label: Scam of the week
sections.title: The "your package couldn't be delivered" text
paragraphs: A text says a package is held up and you need to tap a link to fix the address or pay a small fee. It looks like it came from a delivery company. It didn't.
bullets: You don't have to act. If you're expecting a package, open the delivery company's own app or website yourself, or check the order in your shopping account.
Don't tap the link, and don't reply, not even to say STOP.
Delete the message. If you already tapped it, don't enter any details, and tell someone you trust.

sections.label: Tip of the week
sections.title: Make the text on your phone bigger
paragraphs: You shouldn't have to squint. It takes a minute to fix.
bullets: iPhone: Settings, then Display & Brightness, then Text Size. Slide to the size you like.
Android: Settings, then Display, then Font size. The names vary a little by phone, so type "font size" into the search box at the top of Settings.
sections.note: Menu names change between phone models. If you can't find it, search the Settings app.

sections.label: AI trick of the week
sections.title: Ask AI to say it nicely
paragraphs: Stuck on how to word a tricky message? Tell AI what you want to say, and ask it to make it polite and short.
sections.prompt: Write a kind, short email to my landlord letting him know the kitchen faucet has a steady leak and asking when someone can look at it.
sections.note: Read the result, change anything that doesn't sound like you, and send it yourself. Never type passwords or account numbers into an AI chat.
